summary: 1928 steel tower near Candler; a 1936 paper puts a tower on Spivey Mountain's summit; the 342-acre Spivey Mountain land WLOS reported in 2023 became Buncombe's Deaverview Mountain park land in March 2026, not yet open.

facts.agency: North Carolina Division of Forest Resources

access.note: Buncombe County completed the purchase of the 342-acre Deaverview Mountain property in March 2026. The county has not opened it, and the 2026 report says it is not yet accessible to the public.

events.note: State report: a 35-foot steel tower was erected near Candler. A 1936 item places a tower on Spivey Mountain's summit; the two are not tied together in any source.

evidence.supports: 1928 steel tower, 35 feet, erected near Candler (state biennial report, quoted on the Forest Lookouts page)
evidence.quote: 1928: A 35-foot steel tower was erected near Candler.

evidence.supports: Tower is in Buncombe County (Forest Lookouts page heading)
September 1936 Asheville item: a tower on top of Spivey Mountain at 3,331 feet, the nearest fire tower to Asheville
evidence.quote: On top pf Spivey mountain, 3,331 feet above sea level, stands the nearest forest fire tower to the city of Asheville.

evidence.supports: The 1936 item praises the view from the tower
evidence.quote: The view--an 80 per cent panorama---from the tower is breathtaking and is well worth the short automobile climb from West Asheville.

evidence.supports: 2023: a conservation-minded owner holds 342 acres on Spivey Mountain; county exploring a park
evidence.quote: A conservation-minded individual owns 342 acres on Spivey Mountain and is interested in preserving the land.

evidence.supports: 2023: county leaders are exploring a park on Spivey Mountain
evidence.quote: Buncombe County leaders are exploring creating a park on Spivey Mountain.

evidence.supports: March 2026: county completed purchase of the 342-acre Deaverview Mountain property
evidence.quote: Buncombe County has completed the purchase of the 342-acre Deaverview Mountain property

evidence.supports: The property is not yet accessible to the public
evidence.quote: The property is not yet accessible to the public.

evidence.supports: March 2026 news report: the property includes a 3,118-foot peak
2023: a conservation-minded buyer secured the Deaverview Mountain property (links the 2023 WLOS owner to the 2026 purchase)
evidence.quote: In 2023, a conservation-minded buyer secured the property

evidence.supports: Expected to open eventually for public recreation
evidence.quote: eventually opening it for public recreation and environmental education

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1936 Asheville Citizen-Times item gives the summit as 3,331 feet, while the March 2026 news report describes a 3,118-foot peak on the property. The two may refer to different points or to a different figure; no source reconciles them. The story says so.

The 1928 state report places the tower near Candler. The 1936 item places a tower on the Spivey Mountain summit. Both appear under the Spivey Mountain heading on the Forest Lookouts page, but no source ties them together, so the story does not claim they are the same tower.

sources.title: Spivey Mountain - Forest Lookouts (quoting the state's 1928-30 biennial report and the Asheville Citizen-Times, September 20, 1936)
'Most spectacular view in Asheville:' Creation of park on Spivey Mountain being considered (April 9, 2023)
Buncombe County closes on Deaverview Mountain land (March 20, 2026)

notes_for_editor: The tower's current status is not found in any source. The 1928 Candler tower and the 1936 summit tower are not confirmed as the same structure. The 342 acres in the 2023 WLOS report match the 2026 Deaverview purchase. 828 News NOW says a conservation-minded buyer secured the Deaverview Mountain property in 2023, which links the 2023 owner to the 2026 purchase; the story states this link and says only that the acreage matches the 2023 land. The brief's status (unknown) is not changed. The brief's registers 'NGS' is unverified: the tnlandforms list shows a benchmark code (FB3240) in a column with no label, not a register listing, so it may not belong in registers. The 2023 Spivey Mountain fire in West Asheville is not tied to the tower and was left out.
